description: Import a card or bank statement into an account, through the app’s own pipeline: the same parse, the same dedupe by natural key, the same rules applied on commit. **Dry-runs by default** — it reports what it would import and how the parse compares with the total the file prints for itself, and writes nothing until commit is true. **A file whose printed total does not reconcile is refused**, because importing over it puts numbers in the ledger the file itself says are wrong. Re-importing the same statement is safe: duplicates are matched and skipped.

account_id.description: The account to import into. Ids come from `document_info`. Or `new_account`.

amount_convention.description: One of SIGNED_SINGLE, POSITIVE_IS_CHARGE, SEPARATE_DEBIT_CREDIT. Usually read from the roles you map — state it only when a single amount column needs saying which sign is a charge.

columns.description: Column number → role, from what the user confirmed in `statement_preview`. Omit when a reader already recognises the file.

commit.description: Default false. False previews the import and writes nothing.

file.description: Absolute path to the statement file. One of .xlsx, .xls, .csv.

header_row.description: Force the header row number, when the guess is wrong.

ignore_printed_total.description: Import even though the parse disagrees with the total the file prints. Default false, and it should stay false unless the user is certain the file’s own figure is wrong.

new_account.description: Instead of `account_id`, on a document that has no account for this file yet: the account the statement is for, made on commit — or found, when one of that kind already has these last 4 digits, as the app does when it reads a statement.

last4.description: The last four digits of the card or account.

name.description: A name the user will recognise, e.g. "Cal – Visa 1234".

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

save_mapping_as.description: Keep these columns as a reader under this name, so the next statement of the same shape imports without asking.

sheet.description: Which sheet, when the file has more than one.

name: import_statement
title: Import a statement
